pull_request.title: feat: implement nested_storage_collections lint
pull_request.body:
Closes #42

## Summary

Soroban storage operations are billed on host-object serialization overhead, not just raw byte size. Storing a deeply nested collection (e.g. `Map<Symbol, Map<u32, i128>>`) as a single storage value means that updating a single inner element requires the host to deserialize and re-serialize the *entire* nested structure. This PR adds a lint that catches that pattern at the type level.

- Detects `env.storage()....set(key, value)` calls where the key or the value type is a Soroban `Map`/`Vec` that itself has another `Map`/`Vec` among its generic type arguments (e.g. `Map<Symbol, Map<u32, i128>>`, `Map<Symbol, Vec<i128>>`, `Vec<Map<u32, i128>>`).
- Suggests flattening the structure with a compound key (e.g. a tuple like `(Symbol, u32)`) instead of nesting a second collection.
- A single level of nesting (`Map<Symbol, i128>`, `Vec<i128>`) is **not** flagged — that's the normal, expected shape of Soroban storage.

## Implementation details

Type resolution is done via `rustc_middle::ty::Ty`, not raw HIR type syntax, so it also catches nesting introduced through type aliases resolved by typeck, not just literal `Map<...>` syntax at the call site:

1. On a `.set()` call, resolve the receiver's type via `cx.typeck_results()` and confirm it's one of the existing `SOROBAN_STORAGE_TYPES` (`Instance`/`Persistent`/`Temporary`).
2. Resolve the types of both the key (`args[0]`) and value (`args[1]`) arguments.
3. `has_nested_soroban_collection` peels references, checks the type is a `Map`/`Vec` ADT, then iterates its `GenericArgsRef` (via `arg.as_type()`) and checks whether any generic type argument is *itself* a `Map`/`Vec` (via the new `is_soroban_collection` helper).
4. Both the key and value positions are checked — a collection nested in the key is exactly as expensive to deserialize as one nested in the value.

New constant `SOROBAN_NESTABLE_COLLECTION_TYPES` (`Map`, `Vec`) is separate from the existing `SOROBAN_CONTAINER_TYPES` (`Bytes`, `Vec`, `Map`) since `Bytes` isn't generic over a contained type and can't nest.

## Files

**New:**
- `docs/lints/nested_storage_collections.md` — lint reference page (rationale, example, suggested fix, scope).

**Modified:**
- `soroban_cost_lints/src/lib.rs` — `NestedStorageCollections` late lint pass, `SOROBAN_NESTABLE_COLLECTION_TYPES`, `is_soroban_collection`/`has_nested_soroban_collection` helpers, `LINT_METADATA`/`register_lints` wiring (category: `StorageOperations`).
- `soroban_cost_lints/ui/main.rs` / `ui/main.stderr` — new UI fixtures (see Tests below). The stub `Map`/`Vec` types in the test harness were changed from unit structs to proper `Map<K, V>`/`Vec<T>` generics so nesting can be expressed through the type system; `insert`/`get`/`push_back` keep their prior signatures so the existing `map_insert_in_loop`/`bytes_append_in_loop` fixtures needed only a one-line constructor change (`Map` → `Map::<i32, i32>::new()`, `Vec` → `Vec::new()`) and are otherwise untouched. `Symbol` gained `#[derive(Clone, Copy)]` so a compound-key fixture could reuse it in both a read and a write.
- `README.md`, `docs/lints/README.md`, `docs/cost_rationale.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` — lint listed under Storage Operations with rationale and target-resource summary.

**Test files:** all under `soroban_cost_lints/ui/main.rs` (fixtures) / `soroban_cost_lints/ui/main.stderr` (expected diagnostics), following this repo's existing UI-test convention (no separate test files are used for lints in this crate).

## Tests added

All in the new `nested_storage_collections — Fixtures` section of `ui/main.rs`:

- `bad_map_nested_in_map` — `Map<Symbol, Map<u32, i128>>` → **warns**.
- `bad_vec_nested_in_map` — `Map<Symbol, Vec<i128>>` → **warns**.
- `bad_map_nested_in_vec` — `Vec<Map<u32, i128>>` → **warns**.
- `bad_nested_collection_in_key` — nested collection used as the storage *key* → **warns**.
- `good_flat_map` — `Map<u32, i128>` (one level) → no warning.
- `good_flat_vec` — `Vec<i128>` (scalars only) → no warning.
- `good_compound_key_instead_of_nesting` — flattened `(Symbol, u32)` compound key → no warning.
- `allowed_map_nested_in_map` — same nested case suppressed via `#[allow(nested_storage_collections)]` → no warning.

Each fixture reads the key with `.get()` before writing so the diagnostics stay isolated to this lint rather than incidentally tripping `storage_write_without_read` as well.

## How to test

```bash
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace
```

All three pass locally. The UI test (`cargo test -p soroban_cost_lints`) exercises the new fixtures against the bundled `ui/main.stderr` expectations.

commits.message:
feat: implement nested_storage_collections lint

Detect env.storage()....set() calls whose key or value type nests one
Soroban collection inside another (e.g. Map<Symbol, Map<u32, i128>> or
Map<Symbol, Vec<i128>>). Reading or writing such a value forces the host
to deserialize/re-serialize the whole nested structure even when only a
single inner element changes, so the lint suggests flattening with a
compound key (e.g. (Symbol, u32)) instead.

- Add NestedStorageCollections late lint pass plus is_soroban_collection/
  has_nested_soroban_collection helpers that inspect the generic type
  arguments of Map/Vec via typeck results.
- Add 1-level (non-flagged) and 2+-level (flagged) UI fixtures, including
  nesting in the storage key position and an #[allow] suppression case.
- Generalize the ui test's Map/Vec stubs to be generic over K/V so the
  new fixtures can express real nesting through the type system.
- Document the lint in docs/lints/nested_storage_collections.md, the
  README feature list, docs/lints/README.md, docs/cost_rationale.md, and
  CHANGELOG.md.

Closes #42

Merge remote-tracking branch 'upstream/main' into feat/lint-nested-collections

fix: resolve CI build failures in SARIF output and fixture workspace

- SarifRun.results was typed Vec<SarifResult> while the SARIF result
  builder constructed plain serde_json::Value objects via json!(),
  a leftover mismatch from a prior merge that broke compilation.
  Retype results as Vec<serde_json::Value>, drop the now-dead typed
  Sarif* structs, and wire the already-collected rule descriptors
  into tool.driver.rules.
- integration.rs used HashSet<String> but inserted &str literals;
  fix the declared type.
- alpha/beta fixture crates each declared their own [workspace]
  while also being listed as members of the parent workspace,
  causing cargo metadata to fail with "multiple workspace roots
  found". Drop the redundant per-crate [workspace] tables.

These were the actual cause of the "SARIF result missing level"
CI failures reported on PRs #232, #267, #269, #270 (all inherited
the same broken merge state) — the binary failed to compile, it
was not a runtime field-mapping bug.
